nodes.title: Relative overconvergent Poincaré lemma
nodes.statement: For a separated morphism u of frames inducing an isomorphism on the open scheme, proper on the compactification, and smooth on the formal ambient space near the open scheme, a coherent j†-module E on the target satisfies E ≃ Ru_* DR†_relative(u†E). The relative differential is the canonical one on the pullback; E need not carry an absolute connection for this assertion.
hypotheses: Complete mixed-characteristic DVR V, fraction field K; finite-type separated frames; smoothness is required only near the open scheme.
Use strict neighbourhoods and coherent modules; the completed closed unit disc is not a substitute for the open-disc system.
proofSteps: Use strong fibration to obtain étale local coordinates and a cofinal system of products with discs, retaining the compactification hypotheses.

On one variable, primitive coefficients a_l/(l+1) converge after shrinking the disc radius: for 0<r<1, |1/(l+1)| r^l tends to zero. The differential has constants as kernel. Iterate in the relative coordinates.
Coherent acyclicity on the radius pieces and the cofinality lemmas identify derived direct images with these calculations. Totalize the finite Čech diagram; the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism.

sources.locator: Proposition 8.3.5 and Proposition 8.3.4, pp. 156–162; Lemmas 2.6.3–2.6.8, pp. 76–79
sources.match: The relative de Rham augmentation is an equivalence under these frame hypotheses; radius refinement is part of the proof.

acceptance: A zero-dimensional relative coordinate gives the identity.
Integration is checked on every radius piece; no bounded inverse to differentiation on the closed unit disc is asserted.

nodes.title: Étale-proper de Rham descent
nodes.statement: An étale-proper hypercover of frames is universally of cohomological descent for overconvergent de Rham complexes with overconvergent isocrystal coefficients. For its augmentation ε, the target complex is equivalent to Rε_* of the total simplicial de Rham realization, and the associated first-quadrant spectral sequence computes rigid cohomology.
hypotheses: Open schemes form an étale hypercover; compactifications form the proper part of the frame hypercover.
The coefficient objects have compatible descent data; all totalizations use the cohomological grading convention.
proofSteps: First obtain coherent descent from smooth-proper covers and the standard étale polynomial covers, using local monic-polynomial presentations and their diagonal factorization.
Apply the relative Poincaré equivalence levelwise; filtered relative forms identify the de Rham totalization with the descended coefficient realization.
Use injective resolutions of diagrams and the homotopy uniqueness of their comparison maps to make the augmentation and spectral sequence functorial.

sources.match: Coherent descent and the relative Poincaré lemma yield de Rham descent for étale-proper hypercovers.

acceptance: The constant hypercover yields the identity augmentation.
Replacing a cover by a common refinement gives the same comparison in the derived category.

nodes.title: Exact sequences in rigid coefficients
nodes.statement: For a short exact sequence 0 → E′ → E → E″ → 0 of overconvergent isocrystals on X/K, rigid cohomology has its natural long exact coefficient sequence. The same holds with a fixed closed support Z and with compact support; if the sequence has Frobenius structures, every map is Frobenius compatible.
hypotheses: X is separated of finite type over k; support and compactification conventions are those of the inherited RD.4 complexes.

Use the no-F coefficient refinements of the imported support/localization, MW and finite scalar-extension contracts in this packet; do not obtain arbitrary E∈Isoc† merely by forgetting Frobenius on an F-isocrystal.
proofSteps: Realize the short exact coefficient sequence as coherent j†-modules on a frame; tensoring with locally free forms is exact.
Use exactness of j† and of the supported realization functor before deriving global sections. The short exact sequence of complexes gives a triangle.
Glue by de Rham descent, then take cohomology. Use naturality of the boundary map to retain Frobenius.

nodes.title: Rigid Gysin isomorphism
nodes.statement: If i:Z ↪ X is a closed immersion of smooth separated k-schemes of pure constant codimension c and E is an overconvergent isocrystal on X/K, then RΓ_Z,rig(X/K,E) ≃ RΓ_rig(Z/K,i*E)[−2c]. With compatible q-Frobenius structures this is RΓ_rig(Z/K,i*E)(−c)[−2c]. The comparison is natural for restriction and finite scalar extension. This extends the inherited target restricted to liftable coordinate pairs.
hypotheses: k is perfect of characteristic p, and K is a complete characteristic-zero coefficient field with residue field k.
Mixed codimension components require separate shifts; the Frobenius twist is part of the equivariant statement.
The global coordinate-independence proof is an explicit gap, G1; this node records the full target.

Use the no-F coefficient refinements of the imported support/localization, MW and finite scalar-extension contracts in this packet; do not obtain arbitrary E∈Isoc† merely by forgetting Frobenius on an F-isocrystal.
proofSteps: Reduce smooth closed pairs étale locally to coordinate pairs. Refine the inherited liftable calculation to Taylor-overconvergent coefficients without Frobenius; its no-F coordinate residue map and gluing are explicitly part of G1, rather than an import of the parent’s F-only theorem for an arbitrary E.
The required gluing checks that the residue generator transforms canonically when normal coordinates change, and that the local maps respect support Čech descent. This is the unclosed step in G1.
Use localization for the resulting Gysin sequence; scalar extension is inherited. The divisor example determines the twist sign.

The equivalence is between the formal-completion and special-fibre étale sites; the tube site itself is not asserted equivalent to X_ét.

Compose with the nilpotent/formal invariance of the étale site.
Retain the induced adjunction and the derived pushforward on bounded-below sheaf complexes; restrictions of closed strata give the compatible specialization maps.

Here g*, g_* and f! are exact. There is a canonical natural map F!F* Rs_* → Rs_* f! for the open immersion F:U ↪ X; no general isomorphism or commuting special-fibre endofunctor is included.
hypotheses: The complement tube is the indicated open analytic subspace; f! is an endofunctor on the tube, not extension by zero from ]U[.
proofSteps: Take the kernel of the adjunction unit objectwise in sheaves. Establish exactness using the open tube restriction and direct-image exactness in this setting.
For the natural transformation, factor the unit after Rs_* through the closed special-fibre complement G:X∖U ↪ X. Its restriction after F* vanishes.
Use the kernel universal property to obtain the natural map, and exactness to pass to bounded-below derived complexes.

nodes.title: Log de Rham complexes with proper support
nodes.statement: Fix a Zariski-log scheme (X,L) over κ° and an admissible embedding system (X_•,L_•) ↪ (Z_•,N_•) over W[t]°. Put Y_•=(t=0) in Z_•, with induced log structure M_•. Let u:X_•→X be the hypercover augmentation. Form ω_X=Ru_*Rs_*(Ω•_(Y_•,M_•)/W°⊗O_tube) and its supported version ω_(U,X) by applying f!_(U_•,X_•) inside Rs_*. Form tildeω similarly using Ω•_(Z_•,N_•)/Wtriv⊗O_Y_•. Invert p throughout. The short exact sequence of log form complexes with θ=dlog t and degree-q injection β↦(−1)^(q−1)β∧θ=θ∧β from ω[−1] (whose differential is −d) gives ω[−1]→tildeω→ω→ω and its connecting operator N.
hypotheses: Admissible means: X_• is a Zariski hypercover with exact closed embeddings into finite-type fine log-smooth (Z_•,N_•) over W[t]°. At level zero, (X_0,L_0)≃(Z_0,N_0)×_(W[t]°)κ°; Z_0 is flat and generically smooth over W[t] and smooth over W; Y_0=(t=0) is a relative strict normal-crossings divisor and N_0 is its divisor log structure. Higher levels are induced from these lifts by the embedding-product construction of DL B.1 and GK05 §§5.1–5.2: blow up the componentwise product centre, remove the strict transforms of the component factors, and take the exceptional divisor and lifted diagonal. Arbitrary compatible higher embeddings are not a replacement for this admissible system.

This is a realization after choosing a system. RD.4 supplies its analytic common-refinement comparisons through the log rigid realization; CR.5 supplies log charts and exactification, with the weak-formal extensions explicitly requested. A generic ordinary log connection alone does not supply such a system.
proofSteps: Import log structures, log differentials and exactification from CR.5. Use the semistable local weak lifts and product/refinement construction of the log rigid realization to build the admissible system.

Tensor the absolute and relative log form sequences with analytic tube functions. Apply the exact tube support functor, then derived specialization and hypercover pushforward. Normalize the shifted injection to θ∧β: d(θ∧β)=−θ∧dβ, so it is a chain map from the standard shift with differential −d. The unshifted augmentation to the residue double complex remains β↦β∧θ.
Retain the triangle and its connecting map N as canonical data. Use common admissible refinements and the log Poincaré comparison to identify realizations.

nodes.title: Log residue double complex
nodes.statement: On an admissible system define P_j Ω^m_log as the image of Ω^j_log⊗Ω^(m−j)_regular→Ω^m_log. Put A^(i,j)=Ω^(i+j+1)_log/P_j for i,j≥0, restricted to Y. Its horizontal differential is (−1)^j d and its vertical differential is right wedge α↦α∧dlog t, with total differential their sum. Set P_k A^(i,j)=P_(2j+k+1)Ω^(i+j+1)_log/P_j, with the zero/whole endpoint conventions. The augmentation from relative log forms to Tot A is a quasi-isomorphism; residues identify graded pieces with forms on intersections of irreducible components.
hypotheses: The admissible system and Zariski log structure are those of the supported log complex.
Normal-crossings strata are disjoint unions indexed by unordered subsets of distinct components; use a fixed ordering only to specify incidence signs.
proofSteps: Construct the quotient filtration from wedges of log and ordinary forms. The indicated differentials anticommute by the (−1)^j sign.

nodes.title: Supported log weight spectral sequence
nodes.statement: Write X^(h) for the disjoint union of h-fold intersections of distinct components of proper strictly semistable X, and U^(h)=U×_X X^(h). There is a convergent spectral sequence of underlying K₀-vector spaces E₁^(−k,q+k)=⊕_(j≥max(0,−k)) H_c,rig^(q−2j−k)(U^(2j+k+1)/K₀) ⇒ H^q_rig((U,X)/W°). Its maps to the proper X and boundary spectral sequences are induced by support localization. Tate twists and Frobenius normalization of this page are not specified by this underlying-vector-space statement.
hypotheses: X is proper strictly semistable of finite type over κ°, of pure dimension n−1; the component-intersection and cohomological conventions are fixed above.
No degeneration claim is part of the target. Frobenius-normalized weights belong to RD.6 and require its own residue convention.
proofSteps: Filter the supported residue total complex. Residues compute its graded pieces on component intersections.
Each X^(h) is smooth proper; its nonlog pair support agrees with Berthelot compact support on U^(h).
The finite dimension of the stratum index and bounded-below form complexes give convergence. Natural support maps give the comparison of spectral sequences.

sources.match: Residues give the underlying-vector-space first pages and identify nonlog proper stratum support with ordinary compact support.

acceptance: For one component, this reduces to H_c,rig(U) ⇒ H_rig((U,X)).

nodes.title: Positive log complex with proper support
nodes.statement: Define Ξ^i=Ω^(i+1)_log(Z/Wtriv)/Ω^(i+1)_regular(Z/W), restricted to Y, with the differential inherited from A^(i,0). Put ω⁺_(U,X)=Ru_*Rs_*f!_(U_•,X_•)(Ξ•⊗O_tube). Projection Tot A→A^(•,0)=Ξ• yields ω_(U,X)→ω⁺_(U,X), and the absolute log complex has the compatible map tildeω_(U,X)→ω⁺_(U,X)[−1].
hypotheses: Use the same admissible system and its totalization signs. The superscript + denotes this quotient complex and is not a positivity condition on slopes. For the standard cochain shift, the degree-q absolute quotient map is α↦(−1)^(q−1)[α]∈Ξ^(q−1). Its target differential is −d; the degree signs cancel those of ω[−1]→tildeω in the compatibility square.
proofSteps: Take the j=0 column of the residue double complex.
Project the total complex to its zeroth column; the column-index behavior of the differentials makes this a chain map.

Apply the exact tube support functor and derived pushforwards. The relative map is β↦[β∧θ] without a degree sign. For the absolute map to Ξ[−1], use α↦(−1)^(q−1)[α] in degree q so it commutes with −d on the target and composes with the shifted injection to the shift of the relative map.

sources.locator: Appendix B.2, (B.7)–(B.10), pp. 118–119; Lemma B.6, p. 121
sources.match: The quotient by ordinary forms is the zeroth residue column and receives the supported relative and shifted absolute maps.

acceptance: The quotient has forms of degree i+1 and is indexed in degree i.

nodes.title: Positive support spectral sequence
nodes.statement: There is a convergent spectral sequence E⁺_c,1^(−k,q+k)=H_c,rig^(q−k)(U^(k+1)/K₀) for k≥0 and zero for k<0, abutting to H^q(X_ét,ω⁺_(U,X)). The map from the supported log spectral sequence to this one is projection onto the j=0 summand on E₁.
hypotheses: The strictly semistable proper pair and grading conventions above apply; this is a statement of underlying K₀-vector spaces.
proofSteps: Restrict the residue filtration to the zeroth column.
Compute its graded pieces by the residue isomorphisms; only the intersection order k+1 remains.
The total-to-column projection preserves the filtrations and produces the asserted map on pages and abutments.

For a smooth fibre with one component its sole term is H_c,rig(U).

nodes.title: High-degree comparison for log proper support
nodes.statement: Assume d≥1 and dim(X^(h)∖U^(h))≤d−h for every h≥1. Then H^q_rig((U,X)/W°)→H^q_rig(X/W°) is an isomorphism for q≥2d. The E₁ support comparison in bidegree (−k,q+k) is an isomorphism for q≥2d−|k|. In bidegree (0,2d−1), the direct sum of the j≥1 summands is an isomorphism; the j=0 term is excluded.
hypotheses: An empty stratum is assigned vanishing cohomology and satisfies every dimension bound.
The ordinary rigid vanishing above twice dimension is supplied by RD.4/rigid-support-cohomological-bounds, distinct from the existing RD.5 compact-support-vanishing target.
proofSteps: Use the boundary spectral sequence: degree q−2j−k is above twice the dimension of X^(2j+k+1)∖U^(2j+k+1) for q≥2d−1. This kills boundary cohomology in the two degrees needed for localization.
For pagewise comparison kill both degrees q−2j−k−1 and q−2j−k on each boundary stratum using j≥max(0,−k) and q≥2d−|k|.
At k=0,q=2d−1, the same inequalities hold for j≥1, retaining the stated exception for j=0.

sources.locator: Lemma B.5 and its proof, p. 121
sources.match: Boundary dimension bounds imply the three high-degree comparisons, with a specific excluded j=0 summand.

acceptance: The endpoint q=2d is included.
No isomorphism is asserted for the j=0 summand at degree 2d−1.

nodes.title: Dagger–rigid cohomology comparison
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete mixed-characteristic DVR with fraction field K, and let 𝔓 be a proper admissible formal R-scheme. For Y locally closed in its special fibre, let Q be the dagger structure on the partially proper tube of its closure Ȳ, and let D⊆Q have underlying rigid space ]Y[_𝔓. For a coherent sheaf F on Q, H^q(D,F|_D) ≅ H^q(]Ȳ[_𝔓,j†F′), where F′ is its completion. If D is smooth, the same comparison applies to de Rham hypercohomology. If 𝔓 is smooth near Y, H^i_dR(D) ≅ H^i_rig(Y/K). The comparison is natural for maps of these framed data and intertwines compatible Frobenius lifts; canonical rigid Frobenius follows from lift independence.
hypotheses: The dagger space is the tube equipped with the indicated overconvergent structure, not arbitrary analytification of a nonproper generic fibre.

For a smooth quasi-projective O_K-model use a proper compactification/formal embedding smooth along its special open fibre; its dagger tube supplies D. Coefficients require a coherent connection on Q or descent to a fixed strict neighbourhood before applying the argument.
proofSteps: Use the partially proper dagger/completion equivalence to put Q on the closure tube.

Compare coherent cohomology using finite Čech covers and the two cofinal radius systems in the proof of Theorem 5.1(a). A cocycle is solved after shrinking its individual radius; no uniform choice for all sections is assumed.

Apply the comparison termwise to the coherent differential sheaves; a bounded hypercohomology spectral sequence gives the de Rham comparison. The frame definition of rigid cohomology gives the final identification.
Naturality of completions, forms and radius restrictions gives Frobenius compatibility whenever the maps lift; use the inherited lift-independence theorem for canonical Frobenius.

sources.locator: Theorem 5.1(a)–(c) and proof, pp. 23–24 of arXiv v1; §4.7, p. 21
sources.match: The comparison identifies dagger tube cohomology with j† on the closure tube and, under smoothness, with Berthelot rigid cohomology.

acceptance: For a smooth affine line tube H⁰=K and H^i=0 for i>0.
For the multiplicative-group tube H¹ is the dlog class, with q-Frobenius q; completing to a closed-disc complex cannot replace the dagger restriction.
Maps between proper models which are identical on the special open induce the same rigid comparison by frame independence.

nodes.title: Dagger support and compact-support comparisons
nodes.statement: For a smooth framed Y and closed Z⊆Y, compatible dagger tube realizations identify the supported triangle with the homotopy fibre of RΓ_dR(D_Y)→RΓ_dR(D_(Y∖Z)), hence RΓ_Z,rig(Y/K) with that fibre. Separately, for smooth affine dagger D, use Grosse-Klönne’s definition of compact support via derived sections supported on D inside a larger-radius rigid ambient space, then glue by compact-support excision to obtain RΓ_dR,c(D_Y) ≃ RΓ_c,rig(Y/K). The second comparison, including changes of radius and proper model, is a target with gap G2, not a consequence of ordinary localization alone.
hypotheses: D_Y and D_(Y∖Z) come from one compatible proper formal frame; coefficients descend coherently to the chosen neighbourhoods.
The source compact-support construction uses an ambient support functor and larger-radius presentations. It is not the fibre of ordinary global sections on the open Y.
proofSteps: Apply the ordinary dagger comparison to the two terms of the Z-support localization triangle; its naturality identifies their homotopy fibres.
For compact support import the F1 carrier for larger-radius ambient supported forms and compare its support complex with the inherited RD.4 tube support complex.
Prove invariance under enlarging the ambient radius, then glue via compact-support excision and proper-model independence. The complete proof of these latter comparisons remains G2.

sources.match: Compact support is defined by ambient supported forms for smooth affine dagger spaces; the relation to rigid compact support is announced.
Supports and their excision triangles provide the rigid comparison target.

acceptance: For A¹, ordinary H⁰=K while compact H²=K(−1); replacing compact support by ordinary support localization of A¹ itself fails.
For Z empty the ordinary supported fibre is zero; for Z=Y it is ordinary rigid cohomology.

nodes.title: Log dagger comparison on a fixed admissible model
nodes.statement: Fix an admissible log embedding system with compatible proper formal frames, partially proper dagger closure tubes, and coherent extensions of every log-form term (and, if used, its coherent integrable log coefficient). Derived cohomology of the dagger log-form realization agrees termwise, and after bounded totalization, with the overconvergent j† log-form realization on the closure tubes. This is an ordinary overconvergent comparison. A comparison to the completed DL complexes ω_(U,X), tildeω_(U,X) is conditional on a separate support-preserving dagger-to-convergent adapter for the specified pair and coefficient, compatible with refinements, the signed log triangle and N. For proper X with constant coefficients the unsupported adapter is the proper log rigid/convergent comparison; nonproper boundary and arbitrary log coefficients are not covered by it. The supported adapter and the identification of the HLTT ordinary-locus log complex remain G2.
hypotheses: The proper formal frames, partially proper dagger closure tubes and coherent strict-neighbourhood extensions of the log terms are required data. No termwise sheaf equivalence with completed log forms on an arbitrary nonproper chart is asserted.
Only the fixed-model comparison is asserted; no independence of the proper compactification of log pair cohomology is added.
No weight or finite-slope finiteness conclusion is supplied by this comparison; those import RD.5 and RD.6.

A coherent log connection may be used in the ordinary j† comparison only if every term extends coherently to its dagger closure tube. Its comparison with the completed DL support realization requires the additional coefficient-specific adapter in G2; GK05 Theorem 5.3(ii) here is used only for proper semistable constant coefficients, not for this general log connection.
proofSteps: Apply GK00 Theorem 5.1(a) to coherent log terms on the specified dagger closure tubes. Use its compatible finite Čech/radius realization and natural restriction of the log differential to compare derived cohomology of the bounded complexes. This uses maps of K₀-complexes; the differential is not O-linear. Comparison of completed DL forms is not a consequence of this step.

The signed θ-wedge injection and quotient maps are natural for this ordinary comparison. For proper semistable X with constant coefficients, separately compare dagger and completed realizations by the residue filtration and proper cohomology of each component intersection, using proper-log-rigid-convergent-comparison.

For a supported pair, prove both the ambient dagger/Berthelot support comparison and its compatibility with the completed log-convergent realization, keeping the nonproper boundary convergent. Verify the HLTT log model, horizontal boundary and coefficient extension against these precise complexes. These support/completion/consumer identifications are G2; they are not inferred from the termwise j† comparison.

sources.match: Provides coherent dagger versus overconvergent j† cohomology on the specified proper formal model. Applying it to coherent log terms does not identify completed log-convergent forms on nonproper charts.
The log support realization and its relative/absolute triangle specify the comparison target.

For proper semistable schemes the constant/locally constant log rigid and convergent realizations agree via their proper component intersections; the constant specialization supplies the separate unsupported completed adapter here.

acceptance: A smooth proper model with no horizontal boundary recovers the ordinary proper comparison.
For the standard log point the absolute dlog t class and zero relative monodromy are respected.
For a nonproper open the chosen log compactification remains visible.

nodes.title: Specialization and cospecialization of de Rham cohomology
nodes.statement: Let X be smooth of pure dimension over a complete mixed-characteristic DVR R and admit a smooth proper R-compactification X̄. Let (M,∇) be a coherent algebraic integrable connection on X_K whose dagger restriction M† is overconvergent. Construct ρ_M:RΓ_dR(X_K,M)→RΓ_rig(X_k/K,M†) by analytification and j† restriction, and ρ_c,M:RΓ_c,rig(X_k/K,M†)→RΓ_dR,c(X_K,M) by ambient tube support and rigid GAGA. Algebraic compact support is the derived inverse limit of the boundary-ideal pro-de Rham complexes, independent of a coherent extension of M.
hypotheses: Take a coherent extension M̄ to X̄_K and boundary ideal I; ∇ acts as a connection on the pro-system (I^n M̄)_n, permitting shifts of n, not necessarily on every individual I^n M̄.
Derived inverse limits and rigid coherent GAGA are suppliers; no ordinary inverse limit or single IΩ complex is substituted.
The maps are not asserted to be isomorphisms for nonproper X.
proofSteps: Construct algebraic-to-analytic de Rham restriction, then restrict to the dagger tube coefficient realization to obtain ρ.

Define the compact algebraic complex by Rlim of boundary-ideal powers tensored with forms; change of coherent extension gives a cofinal equivalent pro-system. Rigid GAGA compares its proper global sections with the analytic pro-complex.

Identify tube-supported analytic sections with compact rigid cohomology using the admissible cover by the generic open and boundary tube. Forget the tube support, then use the GAGA comparison to obtain ρ_c.

sources.match: Analytification and overconvergent restriction give specialization, while supported analytic pro-complexes give the opposite-direction cospecialization.

acceptance: The source and target arrows have opposite directions on ordinary and compact support.

hypotheses: Use the pro-complex definition of compact de Rham cohomology and the tube support unit for rigid compact support.
proofSteps: Replace algebraic compact de Rham by its analytic form via proper rigid GAGA.
The support-to-identity unit is natural for restriction to the generic open and the overconvergent realization. Compare the two composites using their adjunction units.
Push forward and apply the inverse GAGA comparison; the resulting diagram is the stated square.

nodes.title: Igusa theta-cokernel interface
nodes.statement: For finite tame level K^p, n≥0 and k≥0, take Pan’s overconvergent modular-form spaces M†_(−k)(K^pΓ(p^n)) and M†_(k+2)(K^pΓ(p^n)) over C, their determinant line D₀, and the geometric differential operator θ_(k+1). Define the finite-level theta cohomology as the algebraic cokernel of θ_(k+1):M†_(−k)→M†_(k+2)⊗D₀^(−k−1). The direct limit over n carries the induced smooth B(Q_p)-action. The comparison of this cokernel with logarithmic rigid cohomology of the Igusa curve with Sym^k coefficient is a separate obligation G3, and its finite-level finiteness imports RD.5 only after that comparison.
hypotheses: C is Pan’s complete algebraically closed characteristic-zero coefficient field. θ includes the determinant twist; its realization is not assumed from an abstract derivative on arbitrary analytic functions.

This node owns the cohomology interface over the supplied geometric data. Construction of modular curves, Igusa level structures and overconvergent modular forms stays with their geometric owners; their realization for Pan’s data is recorded in G3 rather than imported from an upward-tier roadmap.
No finiteness of the infinite-level direct limit is asserted.
proofSteps: Use Mathlib’s quotient by LinearMap.range for the cokernel, with its quotient projection and universal property.

Level-change and Borel maps commuting with θ preserve the image of θ and descend to the quotient. Exactness of filtered colimits of vector spaces identifies the infinite-level cokernel with the direct limit of finite-level cokernels.
Under a change of determinant-line trivialization, use the D₀^(−k−1) factor to intertwine the operators.

To identify the quotient geometrically, construct the logarithmic coefficient de Rham complex and its theta resolution using Coleman’s comparison cited by Pan. This specific realization proof is G3; neither the name H¹_rig nor an abstract quotient proves it.

sources.locator: Definition 5.1.6 and Proposition 5.1.7, pp. 53–54 of arXiv v1; §§5.1.3–5.1.5, p. 53
sources.match: The theta cokernel includes the determinant twist, commutes with the level limit, and receives a geometric log-rigid interpretation for its finiteness claim.

acceptance: Use the quotient interface without redefining the existing generic Mathlib cokernel machinery.

nodes.title: Cohomological bounds for smooth rigid supports
nodes.statement: Let X be smooth separated of finite type over perfect k, with dim X≤d, Z⊆X closed of codimension at least e≥0, and E an overconvergent isocrystal on X/K. Then H^q_Z,rig(X/K,E)=0 for q<2e and for q>2d. In particular H^q_rig(X/K,E)=0 for q>2 dim X by taking Z=X. No coefficient Frobenius is required for this vanishing.
hypotheses: K is the complete mixed-characteristic discrete-valuation coefficient field. Codimension is measured componentwise; the empty support has zero groups in every degree.
This is an amplitude theorem, not finite-dimensionality. It is located in RD.4 because the supported log comparison needs it before RD.5.

Use the no-F coefficient refinements of the imported support/localization, MW and finite scalar-extension contracts in this packet; do not obtain arbitrary E∈Isoc† merely by forgetting Frobenius on an F-isocrystal.
proofSteps: Use induction on ambient dimension and support codimension. Stratify the support into a smooth dense stratum and a higher-codimension remainder, then apply the nested-support exact sequence.

For a smooth support apply the general Gysin comparison: the lower bound follows from the shift 2e, and the upper bound follows inductively from the smaller-dimensional support. Its general gluing obligation is the inherited G1.

For codimension zero, remove an affine open meeting every component and use localization; the complement has positive codimension, where the supported bound has already been proved. On the affine open a smooth weak lift and coherent j† acyclicity reduce ordinary cohomology to a form complex of length at most d. This proves the ambient bound; decompose connected components if their dimensions differ. Finite scalar extension preserves the induction comparisons.

sources.match: The two support-degree bounds are proved by Gysin, excision and dimension induction, for overconvergent coefficients without requiring Frobenius.

acceptance: For a point Z inside A¹, the only possible supported degree is q=2.
For Z=X, e=0 and q>2 dim X vanishes; this makes no finite-dimensionality claim.

nodes.title: Proper log rigid–convergent comparison
nodes.statement: For a proper strictly semistable fine Zariski-log scheme X of pure dimension over κ°, the natural map RΓ_log-rig(X/W°)→RΓ_log-conv(X/W°) is a quasi-isomorphism over K₀. In particular the admissible-system complex ω_X computes log rigid cohomology as well as log convergent cohomology. This statement is for constant coefficients and this proper semistable class; it does not replace the boundary log convergent realization by a rigid one.
hypotheses: κ is finite, W=W(κ), K₀=Frac W, and X is proper over κ.
The two realizations use the same admissible weak lift and its completion, with constant coefficient K₀. Properness of the component intersections supplies the ordinary rigid/convergent comparisons.
proofSteps: Build the residue-filtered double complex for both the weak-formal dagger realization and its completed formal/rigid realization.

Residues identify both first pages with direct sums of shifted cohomology of the same component intersections, using ordinary rigid respectively convergent cohomology. Each intersection is proper and smooth; the inherited ordinary proper comparison identifies these terms.

The natural completion map respects the filtration, residues and augmentations. Comparison of the convergent spectral sequences proves a quasi-isomorphism, identifying the completed admissible-system ω_X with the log rigid realization.

sources.locator: Appendix B.3, p. 119, immediately before Definition B.4
sources.match: The proper strictly semistable case identifies log rigid with log convergent cohomology, citing Grosse-Klönne Theorem 5.3(ii), while boundary terms retain the convergent notation.

Proper component intersections identify the residue spectral sequences of log rigid and log convergent realizations. The coefficient theorem is for Zariski locally constant coefficients; this target uses only the constant coefficient.

acceptance: For the standard log point the comparison identifies K₀ in degree zero.
No comparison is exported for an arbitrary nonproper log boundary.

nodes.title: Log rigid and log convergent realizations
nodes.statement: For a fine κ°-log scheme X admitting a Zariski open cover with exact closed embeddings into log-smooth weak formal W°-schemes, and a finite-rank Zariski locally constant K₀-sheaf E, construct RΓ_log-rig(X/W°,E) from the simplicial dagger tubes of exactifications of the embedding-product diagonals, with coefficient complex sp⁻¹E⊗Ω•_log. The completed-formal/rigid version gives RΓ_log-conv(X/W°,E) and the natural map from the dagger realization. Exactifications and common cover refinements give canonical comparison equivalences. For the strictly semistable class, admissible weak lifts provide the local embedding data.
hypotheses: Use the standard log point κ° and its weak formal Witt lift W°, with K₀=Frac W. Fix the cohomological totalization and alternating cover signs.

Only finite-rank Zariski locally constant coefficients are included in this source realization. A general overconvergent logarithmic connection, including the Sym^k Igusa coefficient, requires the separate G3 realization and cannot use the locally constant coefficient theorem by changing its name.
proofSteps: Choose the local exact log embeddings. For each finite intersection take a product embedding and its exactification, then its dagger tube. The specialization pullback of E tensors with the relative log form complex.

Use the alternating cover diagram and derived global sections to form the realization. Compare choices through product exactifications of a common refinement; the relevant projections are strict and smooth near the embedded scheme, so relative open-polydisc Poincaré gives their quasi-isomorphisms.

Replace weak formal schemes by their completions to obtain the convergent version and the canonical comparison. For a semistable log scheme construct local admissible weak lifts using its normal-crossings embedding and smooth affine lift.

sources.match: Exactifications, relative Poincaré and weak-formal dagger tubes define log rigid cohomology, its comparison with the convergent realization, and semistable embedding data.

acceptance: The coefficient class is explicit in every signature.
The completion map respects the de Rham differential and cover refinements.

inheritedRefinements.statement: A finite module with integrable connection over a weak completion of a smooth V-algebra, equipped with a horizontal invertible Frobenius pullback map lifting residue Frobenius, has the required overconvergent Taylor isomorphism. Integrability without such Frobenius is not enough.
inheritedRefinements.proof: Choose local differential coordinates and a Frobenius-stable integral lattice. The derivative of a Frobenius lift is π-divisible, so iterating its horizontal isomorphism makes the connection matrices integral. On a Banach radius near one the normalized iterated derivatives converge for a small Taylor radius. Frobenius extends that radius by η_(n+1)=min(η_n^(1/p),η_n/c), |π|<c<1, so η_n tends to one; shrink the coefficient radius at each stage. Horizontality makes the expansions agree, giving the overconvergent diagonal stratification.
